result: In 20 CFS women vs 20 sedentary controls, accelerometer-measured average activity fell significantly in the week after a maximal treadmill test, most on days 12-14 of monitoring, with a longer waking day and more daily rests.
reason: Objective activity measure of delayed post-exertional decline adds an actigraphy time course to the PEM timing finding.

result: Serum acylcarnitine was low in 57 Swedish CFS patients vs 46 controls (p<0.001), replicating earlier Japanese data; among other diseases only chronic hepatitis C also showed low acylcarnitine.
reason: Independent cohort, same serum carnitine measure, same direction.

result: With a 1 microgram ACTH test in 20 CFS vs 20 controls, baseline cortisol did not differ but the cortisol increment was lower in CFS, and 45% vs 10% failed a 250 nmol/l cutoff.
reason: Same ACTH challenge measure, blunted cortisol response as claimed.

result: After 100 microg ovine CRH in 14 CFS patients without psychiatric illness vs 14 controls, ACTH (P<0.005) and cortisol (P<0.05) release were blunted with equal basal values.
reason: CRH rather than ACTH challenge; blunted ACTH points to a pituitary-level contribution, so it extends the challenge-test finding rather than replicating it.

result: 24-h salivary and urinary cortisol did not differ between 22 CFS patients and controls.
reason: Same salivary and urinary free cortisol measures, null result.

result: In 14 unmedicated CFS women vs 131 healthy and 26 depressed controls, evening salivary cortisol was lower in CFS (P=0.005 vs healthy, P=0.02 vs depressed), and morning cortisol was lower in CFS without psychiatric disorder (P=0.009).
reason: Same salivary cortisol measure, lower in CFS; small sample.

result: Urinary free cortisol was significantly lower in 21 CFS patients than in 15 healthy controls and higher in 10 melancholic depressives; CFS patients with comorbid depression kept the low profile.
reason: Same 24-h urinary free cortisol measure, same direction.

result: Brain MRI was abnormal in 32% of 43 CFS patients and 28% of 43 matched controls, and white matter hyperintensity prevalence did not differ.
reason: Routine clinical MRI reads show no CFS-specific abnormality, consistent with the null finding.

result: 22 of 78 CFS patients had delayed orthostatic hypotension on tilt; after salt therapy 11 normalised, while the 10 who stayed tilt-positive had lower plasma renin activity (0.79 vs 1.29 pmol/ml/h in controls, 1.0 in responders; p=0.04).
reason: Low renin only in a salt-nonresponsive orthostatic subgroup, with no blood volume or aldosterone measured; adds a subgroup rather than replicating the paradox.
